results.title: African CEOs remain confident in growth, but economic uncertainty, AI readiness will shape next phase of investment – KPMG
results.content: The findings point to a business environment in which ambition remains strong, but execution is becoming increasingly important. While 66% of African CEOs are confident in the global economy, broadly in line with the global benchmark of 65%, confidence in their domestic economies stands at 72%. A further 79% are confident in the growth prospects of their own organisations.

results.title: MTN’s profit before tax for Q3 hits GH¢ 11.3 billion
results.content: The figure represents a 51.8% jump over the GH¢ 7.7 billion it recorded during the same period in 2025.

results.title: 5th Edition of Ghana Corporate Brands Conference and Honours launched
results.content: Under the theme, "Shaping the Future of Corporate Branding in Ghana: Building Brands with Strategic Intent, Inspiring Excellence, and Earning Lasting Trust", the event is expected to convene key voices from business, academia and industry to discuss emerging branding trends, reputation management, customer expectations and the growing role of technology in shaping public perception.

results.title: NAIMOS targets suppliers of equipment used in illegal mining in Aowin and Enchi
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has announced plans to target individuals and businesses manufacturing or selling equipment used in illegal mining as part of efforts to curb galamsey in Aowin and Enchi in the Western North Region. Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel S. K. Appiah, said the taskforce would focus on the supply chain supporting illegal mining activities in addition to enforcement against operators. Speaking during a tour of the taskforce’s operations in the area, he said the objective was to enforce the law and halt the destruction of the environment without unnecessarily undermining legitimate livelihoods. “We are not here to destroy livelihoods, but to enforce the law,” he said.

results.title: We’re satisfied with Afenyo-Markin’s leadership in Parliament; rules out changes to Minority leadership – NPP
results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) says it is satisfied with the work of the Minority leadership in Parliament under Alexander Afenyo-Markin and has no plans to replace him.

results.title: Ghana reviews employment policy to identify green job opportunities
results.content: Ghana is reviewing its National Employment Policy to address emerging labour market challenges and identify opportunities for creating decent jobs through the green economy.

results.title: Farmer Globale earns international recognition for climate-smart rice farming
results.content: A Ghanaian agribusiness company, Farmer Globale, has earned international recognition at the Africa Sustainable Futures Awards, hosted by the Financial Times in partnership with the World Bank Group’s Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) in the United Kingdom on October 21 and 22, 2026.

results.title: Ghana and Poland explore investment opportunities and security cooperation
results.content: Ghana and Poland have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations, with discussions focusing on trade, investment, industrial development, technology, education and security.

results.title: Stakeholders call for stronger community-security collaboration to prevent extremism
results.content: Stakeholders have called for stronger collaboration between communities and security agencies to prevent violent extremism and safeguard Ghana’s peace.

results.title: GJA pushes for bill to establish minimum wage for journalists
results.content: The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) is seeking to lay a private-member bill before parliament that would consider improving the economic and working conditions of journalists.

results.title: NDC’s Tanko Computer dismisses NPP denial of alleged plot to remove Afenyo-Markin
results.content: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has dismissed the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) denial of reports that it is planning to change its Minority leadership in Parliament, describing the response as “fire fighting”. Speaking on JoyNews’ Top Story, NDC member Rashid Tanko Computer said the alleged plan to remove Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin had been discussed since the 2024 general elections. He insisted that the governing party was not seeking to influence the NPP’s leadership decisions but maintained that the opposition party was responding to mounting pressure following the reports. “Are they not fire fighting? That’s what they are doing. We are not determining for them. We are not telling them they should change their leaders or not. From the outset, they wanted to remove him,” he said.

results.title: La residents petition Mahama over Laboma, Kajano and Labadi Beach demolitions
results.content: Hundreds of protesters from La communities have petitioned President John Dramani Mahama over the demolition of businesses at Laboma, Kajano and Labadi Beach, demanding compensation and government intervention to address the loss of livelihoods. The demonstration, dubbed “Aaagbe Wɔ”, meaning “They are killing us”, was organised by the Ga-Dangme Progressive Front on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The protesters, including affected business owners, residents and supporters, marched to Jubilee House to demand justice, engagement with stakeholders and clarity on the future of the demolished sites. They said the demolitions had destroyed businesses built over several years, leaving owners, workers and their families facing economic hardship.

results.title: Petrol price to drop by 3.51%, while diesel will go up by 1.50% from Nov. 1 – COMAC
results.content: Petrol prices are expected to fall by up to 3.35% per litre from November 1, 2026, while diesel prices could rise by 1.50%, according to the Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies (COMAC).

results.title: Only 7.7% of Ghana’s 2.64m businesses operate formally – Government Statistician
results.content: Government Statistician Dr Alhassan Iddrisu says only 7.7% of Ghana’s 2.64 million businesses were operating formally in 2024, highlighting persistent challenges in business formalisation and job creation.

results.title: UCC postpones reopening for Level 100 distance education students to November 23
results.content: The University of Cape Coast (UCC) has postponed the reopening date for Level 100 students of its College of Distance Education (CoDE) for the 2026/2027 academic year.

results.title: Ashanti Regional GJA secures land waiver for proposed press centre
results.content: The Ashanti Regional Branch of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has secured a waiver on land allocated by Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II for the proposed Ashanti Press Centre, marking a significant milestone in efforts to establish a permanent office for journalists in the region.

results.title: Asene farmers demand compensation for farms destroyed by Accra-Kumasi expressway
results.content: More than 200 farmers at Akyem Asene, near Oda in the Eastern Region, have appealed to the government to pay them adequate compensation for their farms and plantations destroyed to make way for the construction of the new Accra-Kumasi expressway.

results.title: Divided by Party, United in Suffering: Ghana’s dilemma of blind partisan loyalty
results.content: There is something deeply troubling about the way politics has come to occupy Ghana’s public space. Every morning, from television and radio programmes to conversations in taxis, offices and homes, we encounter the same political theatre.

results.title: Prisons Council explores legal aid for inmates over challenges with appeals
results.content: The Chairman of the Ghana Prisons Service Council, Apostle Ing. Alexander Nana Yaw Kumi-Larbi, has disclosed plans to explore legal assistance for inmates, following concerns over difficulties in accessing court proceedings and securing legal representation for appeals.

results.title: Ghanaian neuroscientist honoured at Millennium Excellence Awards USA for Alzheimer’s blood test discovery
results.content: Thomas Karikari, associate professor of psychiatry and clinical and translational science at the University of Pittsburgh’s School of Medicine in the United States, was a proud recipient of the Excellence in Scientific Research award at the recent Millennium Excellence Awards ceremony in Washington, DC, under the royal patronage of Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, the Asantehene.

results.title: Mahama appoints 15 officers of the Ghana Prisons Service
results.content: President John Mahama has promoted 15 officers of the Ghana Prisons Service, elevating seven Deputy Directors of Prisons to Directors of Prisons and eight Assistant Directors of Prisons to Deputy Directors of Prisons.

results.title: Minerals Commission defends termination of Northern Ashanti Mines’ mineral rights over $8.3m debt
results.content: The Minerals Commission has defended its decision to terminate the mineral rights of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited, formerly Owere Mines, insisting that the company persistently failed to meet its statutory financial obligations despite several opportunities to settle its debts.

results.title: Women domestic workers earn 48% of other employees’ wages – ILO
results.content: Women employed as domestic workers worldwide earn an average of 48% of the monthly wages of other employees, highlighting persistent gender-based inequalities in the sector, according to the International Labour Organization (ILO).

results.title: Africa records 4.2 million increase in domestic workers since 2019 – ILO
results.content: Africa recorded an increase of 4.2 million domestic workers between 2019 and 2025, the largest rise among the world's regions, according to the International Labour Organization (ILO).

results.title: Ghana at risk of missing 2030 methane emissions target, AMA warns, as stakeholders push for more funding and waste separation
results.content: Ghana risks missing its target of cutting methane emissions from the waste sector by 30 percent by 2030, officials of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) have warned, citing funding shortfalls and weak waste collection. The warning came on Wednesday at the Accra LOW-M Institutional and Climate Finance Roundtable at the Africa Regent Hotel in Accra. The event was organised by the AMA and the Green Africa Youth Organization (GAYO), with the Global Alliance for Incinerator Alternatives (GAIA) and C40 Cities. It brought together the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, the Ministry of Finance, the Environmental Protection Agency and its Ghana Carbon Markets Office, the private sector and informal waste workers. results.title: NPP rejects reports of changes to Minority leadership in parliament
results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has rejected reports that it is considering changes to its parliamentary leadership, saying no discussions have taken place to replace Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin and his team.

results.title: GAYO, AMA hold roundtable to secure funding and institutional backing for Accra’s methane reduction plan
results.content: The Green Africa Youth Organization (GAYO) and the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) have held a roundtable to get government institutions and funders to commit to Accra's plan to cut methane emissions from waste. The Accra LOW-M Institutional and Climate Finance Roundtable: Advancing Coordinated Action and Climate Finance for Urban Methane Reduction, held on Wednesday at the Africa Regent Hotel in Accra, focused on the Accra LOW-M (Lowering Organic Waste Methane) Portfolio. The plan aims to cut methane emissions from the city’s waste by at least 30 percent by 2030, mainly by turning organic waste into compost and biogas instead of sending it to landfills. results.title: More than 80% of domestic workers worldwide remain in informal employment – ILO
results.content: More than four in five domestic workers worldwide remain in informal employment, often without effective labour and social protection, despite progress in many countries, a new report by the International Labour Organization (ILO) has found.

results.title: La General Hospital project expected to be completed by end of 2027 – Health Minister
results.content: Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh says the La General Hospital project, valued at €50 million, is expected to be completed by the end of 2027, with about €15 million paid so far.
